why: THE SHADOWING TRAP, which is why this gate resolves an action to the bindings it REALLY has. Declaring an action in `[input]` REPLACES its built-in default rather than adding to it, so this -- a `ui_up` that keeps the WASD event and loses the arrow event -- is exactly the edit that silently kills the arrow keys. A gate that only asked "is the action declared" would pass on it, and the HUD would advertise arrows that no longer move anything.

break: node scripts/edit.mjs godot/scripts/main.gd --anchor 'hint.text = "Esc / P to resume"' --replace 'hint.text = "Esc / P / W to resume"'
why: A VACUOUS RESUME CLAIM, and the gate published one as proof of coverage. `Esc / P to resume` edited to `Esc / P / W to resume` -- W bound to movement and to nothing else -- used to exit 0, because the probe tapped the key twice from PLAYING and asked only whether the state was PLAYING after the SECOND tap: a question a key that does nothing answers correctly (`toggle key=W playing=1 after_first=1 after_second=1`). The key is now pressed while the run is PAUSED, so the verdict is about resuming. `requires: godot` because the failure is produced by DRIVING the game; where the engine is absent the probe does not run and the self-test would blame the gate for a missing dependency.

break: node scripts/edit.mjs godot/scripts/main.gd --anchor 'b.pressed.connect(_on_pick.bind(i))' --replace 'b.pressed.connect(_on_pick.bind(0))'
why: ONLY THE FOCUSED CONTROL WAS EVER PRESSED. Binding every picker button to `_on_pick.bind(0)` makes two of the three offered upgrades apply the wrong upgrade, and this gate used to exit 0: the probe tapped `ui_accept` at whatever had focus, and on the picker that is always `Pick0`. Each offered control is now pressed in its own run and the offer it applied is identified against the game's own `Upgrades.apply`. `requires: godot` for the same reason as the entry above.

	_lower_shade()' --replace '	picker.visible = false
	push_warning("remember to call _lower_shade() sometime")'
why: A MESSAGE IS NOT A LOWERING. The `_lower_shade()` call is replaced by a warning that merely NAMES it, so the dim is never lowered -- and the gate used to exit 0, because the call graph was built from name TOKENS and a name inside a string literal counted as an edge. String contents are stripped before the token graph is built now, so the mention is not a call.
